argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Transcendental-critical analysis of the conditions of moral obligation, combined with a dialectical resolution of an antinomy.
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate: premises are embedded in conceptual contrasts rather than formalized step-by-step.

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High: the text stages a genuine conflict between eudaimonism and Kantian autonomy and resolves it through the highest good.
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High: each section directly advances the thesis that happiness cannot ground morality but can be its rational consequence.
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate: the Kantian premises are asserted rather than independently defended; the text assumes the categorical imperative and autonomy as starting points.

explicit_definitions_given: happiness: aggregate of subjective satisfactions, desires, and inclinations
categorical imperative: command of pure practical reason, unconditional and universal
autonomy: will giving itself the moral law
heteronomy: will determined by external/empirical object
highest good: proportionate union of virtue and happiness

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: The text anticipates the objection that excluding happiness from morality makes moral life futile; it responds by postulating the highest good as a rational completion.
objections_raised: If happiness is excluded from morality, the moral life seems futile.
If happiness is included as motive, morality becomes heteronomous.

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, transcendental argument, practical postulates; no empirical evidence.

structural_organization.structure_type: Recursive amplification: each section restates and extends the previous thesis, culminating in a synthesis.

summary_of_core_decisions: The text rejects eudaimonism by distinguishing happiness from moral worth, grounds morality in the categorical imperative and autonomy, redefines happiness as worthiness rather than motive, and resolves the antinomy of practical reason through the postulate of the highest good.

thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Low: final paragraph states the conclusion without qualification.
